scenes.tts: Before netrin had a name, a worm held the clue. How can one cue send cells in two directions?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Worm Already Knew. A worm with arrows pointing both toward and away from its ventral side. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Before netrin had a name, a worm held the clue. How can one cue send cells in two directions?

scenes.tts: Start on the spinal cord map, then switch to the worm. There, U N C six is made on the ventral side.
scenes.caption: Start on the spinal cord map, then switch to the worm. There, UNC-6 is made on the ventral side.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. The map slides aside for a worm cross-section with a glowing ventral band. Label: UNC-6, ventral.
scenes.narration: Start on the spinal cord map, then switch to the worm. There, UNC-6 is made on the ventral side.

scenes.tts: The worm C elegans is transparent. Many of its cells can be named and found again in every animal.
scenes.caption: The worm C. elegans is transparent. Many of its cells can be named and found again in every animal.
scenes.visual: A transparent worm with a few named cells tagged; the same tags appear on a second worm.
scenes.narration: The worm C. elegans is transparent. Many of its cells can be named and found again in every animal.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety, Edward Hedgecock and colleagues followed migrating cells and pioneer axons.
scenes.caption: In 1990, Edward Hedgecock and colleagues followed migrating cells and pioneer axons.
scenes.visual: Label: 1990, Hedgecock and colleagues. Cells and axons trace paths around the worm.
scenes.narration: In 1990, Edward Hedgecock and colleagues followed migrating cells and pioneer axons.

scenes.tts: Pioneer axons are the first axons to lay down a route.
scenes.visual: A single axon grows first along an empty route; later axons follow it. Label: pioneer axon.
scenes.narration: Pioneer axons are the first axons to lay down a route.

scenes.tts: Some cells move toward the ventral side. Others move away from it.
scenes.visual: Two arrows on the worm section: one down toward the ventral band, one up toward the dorsal side.
scenes.narration: Some cells move toward the ventral side. Others move away from it.

scenes.tts: The team looked at mutants of three genes. The first was unc six, the gene for the cue itself.
scenes.caption: The team looked at mutants of three genes. The first was unc-6, the gene for the cue itself.
scenes.visual: A table appears with three empty rows: unc-6, unc-40, unc-5. Columns: toward ventral, away from ventral.
scenes.narration: The team looked at mutants of three genes. The first was unc-6, the gene for the cue itself.

scenes.tts: Lose the cue. Which migrations should fail: toward the ventral side, away from it, or both?
scenes.visual: The unc-6 row is highlighted, both cells empty. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Lose the cue. Which migrations should fail: toward the ventral side, away from it, or both?

scenes.tts: Both. Without U N C six, many migrations in both directions went the wrong way. The cells and axons still moved, but misdirected.
scenes.caption: Both. Without UNC-6, many migrations in both directions went the wrong way. The cells and axons still moved, but misdirected.
scenes.visual: The unc-6 row fills: disrupted, disrupted. Both arrows on the worm still move but wander off course.
scenes.narration: Both. Without UNC-6, many migrations in both directions went the wrong way. The cells and axons still moved, but misdirected.

scenes.tts: Mutants of unc forty failed mainly in movement toward the ventral side. Movement away was largely normal.
scenes.caption: Mutants of unc-40 failed mainly in movement toward the ventral side. Movement away was largely normal.
scenes.visual: The unc-40 row fills: mainly fails, largely normal. The downward arrow greys.
scenes.narration: Mutants of unc-40 failed mainly in movement toward the ventral side. Movement away was largely normal.

scenes.tts: Mutants of unc five showed the mirror image. They failed mainly in movement away.
scenes.caption: Mutants of unc-5 showed the mirror image. They failed mainly in movement away.
scenes.visual: The unc-5 row fills: largely normal, mainly fails. The upward arrow greys.
scenes.narration: Mutants of unc-5 showed the mirror image. They failed mainly in movement away.

scenes.tts: One cue, two readers, two directions. Unc forty reads toward. Unc five reads away.
scenes.caption: One cue, two readers, two directions. unc-40 reads toward. unc-5 reads away.
scenes.visual: A reading column appears: no cue; the toward reader; the away reader. Banner: one cue, two readers.
scenes.narration: One cue, two readers, two directions. unc-40 reads toward. unc-5 reads away.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-two, U N C six turned out to be a laminin-related protein. U N C five turned out to span the membrane.
scenes.caption: In 1992, UNC-6 turned out to be a laminin-related protein. UNC-5 turned out to span the membrane.
scenes.visual: Label: 1992. UNC-6 drawn as a laminin-like protein; UNC-5 drawn crossing a membrane.
scenes.narration: In 1992, UNC-6 turned out to be a laminin-related protein. UNC-5 turned out to span the membrane.

scenes.tts: The table links genes to directions. To test the link, change the reader and leave the cue alone.
scenes.visual: The table shrinks to a corner. A dial labelled reader turns while a dial labelled cue stays fixed.
scenes.narration: The table links genes to directions. To test the link, change the reader and leave the cue alone.

scenes.tts: Worm touch neurons do not normally carry U N C five. Their axons do not grow dorsally.
scenes.caption: Worm touch neurons do not normally carry UNC-5. Their axons do not grow dorsally.
scenes.visual: A touch neuron on the worm with its axon running along the body. Label: no UNC-5.
scenes.narration: Worm touch neurons do not normally carry UNC-5. Their axons do not grow dorsally.

scenes.tts: Force them to make U N C five. Which way do their axons grow? And does the new route still need U N C six?
scenes.caption: Force them to make UNC-5. Which way do their axons grow? And does the new route still need UNC-6?
scenes.visual: The touch neuron gains UNC-5 receptors on its growth cone. Question on screen: which way, and does it need UNC-6?
scenes.narration: Force them to make UNC-5. Which way do their axons grow? And does the new route still need UNC-6?

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-three, Michel Hamelin and colleagues did this. The axons grew dorsally, away from the ventral U N C six.
scenes.caption: In 1993, Michel Hamelin and colleagues did this. The axons grew dorsally, away from the ventral UNC-6.
scenes.visual: Label: 1993, Hamelin and colleagues. The touch-neuron axon turns and grows dorsally, away from the ventral band.
scenes.narration: In 1993, Michel Hamelin and colleagues did this. The axons grew dorsally, away from the ventral UNC-6.

scenes.tts: And the new route still needed U N C six.
scenes.caption: And the new route still needed UNC-6.
scenes.visual: With the ventral band removed, the dorsal turn disappears. Label: still needs UNC-6.
scenes.narration: And the new route still needed UNC-6.

scenes.tts: The cue never changed. It marked the ventral side throughout. The receptor set the direction.
scenes.visual: The ventral band stays fixed while the receptor on the growth cone swaps; the arrow flips with it.
scenes.narration: The cue never changed. It marked the ventral side throughout. The receptor set the direction.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: changing the receptor changed the answer to an unchanged cue.
scenes.visual: Return to the spinal cord map; box 2 begins to fill. Takeaway on screen: change the receptor, change the answer.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: changing the receptor changed the answer to an unchanged cue.
